content: The right main bronchus, also referred to as the right primary bronchus or right principal bronchus, is anatomically wider, shorter, and more vertically oriented compared to the left main bronchus.5 cm in length and enters the right lung at a level nearly corresponding to the fifth thoracic vertebra. The azygos vein arches over the right main bronchus from behind, while the right pulmonary artery is initially positioned below it and later courses anteriorly. Approximately 2 cm from its origin, the right main bronchus gives rise to a branch that supplies the upper lobe of the right lung. This branch is known as the eparterial bronchus because it originates superior to the right pulmonary artery. Beyond this point, the bronchus passes inferior to the pulmonary artery and is referred to as the hyparterial bronchus. The hyparterial bronchus subsequently bifurcates into two branches, which supply the middle and lower lobes of the right lung.
